summary: Česnavičius proves purity for the Brauer group: for a regular scheme X and a closed subset Z of codimension at least 2, H²(X, G_m) → H²(X∖Z, G_m) is an isomorphism, settling the remaining mixed-characteristic p-primary case through finite-flat descent, henselian completion and perfectoid techniques, with refinements for tori and a characterization of fields of dimension at most one. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and four findings are recorded; Proposition 2.2 is not established for noncommutative G (E1), which the main theorems do not need. Not formalised.
conventions: Rings are commutative with unit; regular local means Noetherian regular local, as in the pinned class.
H^q denotes étale cohomology unless explicitly marked fppf; nonabelian H^1 is a pointed set, not an abelian group.
Br'(X)=H²_et(X,G_m)_tors is distinguished from all of H²; Br'(X)=H² only with a proved torsion theorem.
U_R removes every closed point when R is semilocal. In towers use the actual inverse-limit open, not a fictitious Noetherian spectrum.
p is prime; the paper's perfectoid convention always includes p-torsion freeness. The broader BMS integral-perfectoid notion remains the shared owner.
Statements/lemma names below are planning interfaces, not Lean declarations. Every test is unexecuted.
Source routes refine named existing stages; dependencies are item-level prefixes/suffixes, not blanket reverse edges between entire roadmaps.

Elkik §§0–II is Noetherian throughout. GR5.4.8 and the direct finite-conormal step allow arbitrary R but require t regular. H_Jac⊂H_fac=H_R uses a comparison; the first containment is not replaced by equality.

This abelian case is what Propositions 2.2 (commutative specialization), 2.3 and Corollary 2.4 use.

Deduce exactness of π_* on abelian étale sheaves (SGA4 VIII 5.5) and the Leray comparison of H¹.

items.name: Finite-flat H¹ injectivity (printed scope pending proof check)
items.statement: For a finite flat map of local rings R→R', an open V⊂Spec R, and a smooth affine R-group G, assume Γ(R,O)→Γ(V,O) is an isomorphism and every G-torsor on R is trivial. Proposition 2.2 states H¹_et(V,G)→H¹_et(V_(R'),G) is injective.
proofSteps: Extend Q(V) to Q(R) by the affine/Hartogs adjunction.
Lift Q(R) to Res G(R) using H¹(R,G)=*.
This proves the neutral fibre is trivial. Full pointed-set injectivity requires the twisted-fibre argument in Gir71 III3.2.2; not certified here.
items.note: The later uses have commutative G, where kernel-triviality suffices; they depend on h1-abelian, not on this item. No other item depends on this one. The printed proof checks only that H(V)→X(V) is surjective, which is the untwisted case. Full pointed-set injectivity for noncommutative G would also need surjectivity of the twisted maps (^P H)(V)→(^P X)(V) for G-torsors P on V that do not extend to R. This is recorded as research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19.json, E1 (gap). It is an open proof gap, not a claimed counterexample.

items.name: Quantitative approximate-root improvement
items.statement: Let t be regular in R, I⊂R an ideal, S=F/J as above, a∈R^N and p_a=(X_i−a_i). If t^h∈H_R(F,J)+p_a, J⊂p_a+t^n IF and n>2h, there is b with b−a∈t^(n−h)IR^N and J⊂p_b+(t^(n−h)I)²F.
proofSteps: Worker-derived direct proof: choose h₀∈H_R(F,J) with h₀(a)=t^h. Via factor-ideal-comparison choose u:S^N→J/J² with u d=h₀ id. Lift u(dX_k) to b_k∈J.
For every generator f_i, h₀f_i−Σ_k(∂_k f_i)b_k∈J². Evaluation gives t^h f_i(a)−Σ_k Jac_ik(a)b_k(a)∈t^(2n)I²; also b_k(a)∈t^nI.
Write b_k(a)=t^hδ_k with δ_k∈t^(n−h)I. Regularity of t implies f_i(a)−Σ_k Jac_ik(a)δ_k∈t^(2n−h)I²⊂t^(2n−2h)I².
The multivariate Taylor remainder at a−δ lies in (t^(n−h)I)². Thus b=a−δ has the required correction and error. This finite polynomial step needs neither Noetherianity nor completeness.

Alternative source proof: GR3.2.16 constructs ω∈Ext¹(L,t^nI/(t^nI)²); the square of maps α,β,γ,δ in GR5.4.8 transfers t^hω=0 to αω=0. The full morphism-obstruction theorem is optional for the direct finite-conormal proof, but the H_R-to-H_fac dictionary still imports DD.0.

items.name: Finiteness theorem for local cohomology (SGA 2 VIII 2.1)
items.statement: Let X be a locally Noetherian prescheme that is locally embeddable in a regular prescheme, Y a closed part of X, F a coherent O_X-module and i an integer; put U = X - Y and c(x) = codim(closure{x} ∩ Y, closure{x}). If H^{i-c(x)}(F_x) = 0 for every x ∈ U, where H^•(F_x) is local cohomology at the maximal ideal of O_{X,x}, then H^i_Y(F) is coherent.

Feed d) into the biduality spectral sequence of SGA 2 VIII §1 to obtain coherence of H^i_Y(F).

items.name: Depth criteria for coherence of local cohomology (SGA 2 VIII 2.3)
items.statement: Let X be locally Noetherian and locally embeddable in a regular prescheme, Y a closed part of X, F a coherent O_X-module, n an integer, U = X - Y and c as above. items.name: Formal comparison of sections on a punctured spectrum (SGA 2 IX 1.4 and 1.5)

items.name: Infinitesimal Picard obstruction sequence (SGA 2 XI 1.1)
items.statement: Let X be locally Noetherian, I a quasi-coherent ideal, Y = V(I), X_n = (Y, O_X/I^{n+1}) and P_n = I^{n+1}/I^{n+2}. items.name: Picard descent along a regular hypersurface section (SGA 2 XI 3.16 and 3.17)
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian local ring that is a quotient of a regular ring, t ∈ r(A) an A-regular element, and suppose A is complete for the t-adic topology. Put X_0 = Spec A, Y_0 = V(t) = Spec(A/tA), x = r(A), X = X_0 - {x}, Y = Y_0 - {x}. (3.16) If (a) prof O_{X,y} ≥ 2 for every y closed in X and (b) prof A/tA ≥ 3, then Pic(X) → Pic(Y) is injective; in particular A is parafactorial as soon as A/tA is. (3.17) If moreover (c) prof O_{X,y} ≥ 3 for every y closed in Y, (d) prof A/tA ≥ 4, and (e) O_{X,y} is parafactorial for every closed point y of X that does NOT lie in Y, then Pic(X) → Pic(Y) is an isomorphism, and A is parafactorial if and only if A/tA is.
items.locator: SGA 2 XI Lemme 3.16 and Lemme 3.17, read with their proofs and with the proof of Théorème 3.13 (ii), on 2026-09-22
proofSteps: Hypothesis (a) gives Lef(X, Y) and (a) with (c) gives Leff(X, Y), by SGA 2 X Example 2.1.

Since t is A-regular, P_n = (I^{n+1}/I^{n+2})|Y ≅ O_Y for every n, so the vanishing needed from XI 1.1 reduces to H^1(Y, O_Y) = 0, resp. H^i(Y, O_Y) = 0 for i = 1, 2; the excision sequence H^i(Y_0, O) → H^i(Y, O) → H^{i+1}_x(Y_0, O) gives it from (b), resp. (d), because Y_0 is affine.

For 3.17 conclude with XI Proposition 3.12, whose third hypothesis is supplied by (e): for every open neighbourhood U of Y in X the complement X - U is a finite set of closed points of X, and those points lie outside Y.

Deduce Théorème 3.13 (ii) by induction on the length of the regular sequence presenting a local complete intersection of dimension ≥ 4, the base case being regular local rings, which are factorial by 3.13 (i) and hence parafactorial by 3.10.

uses.how: Uses the hypersurface Picard descent to run the induction on the length of the regular sequence that presents a local complete intersection of dimension at least four.

proofSteps: Faithfulness: two maps f_i, g_i : Y_i → Y'_i that agree after pullback to X have graphs Γ_{f_i}, Γ_{g_i} : Y_i ↪ Z_i = Y_i ×_{X_i} Y'_i, which are immersions and hence determined by their quasi-compact open images in |Z_i|; since |Z| = lim_j |Z_j| by 6.4 (o), two quasi-compact opens that agree over |Z| already agree over some |Z_j|.

Intermediate step: if f_i : Y_i → Y'_i pulls back to an isomorphism over X, then it is an isomorphism over X_j for large j — its image is a quasi-compact open through which Y' → Y'_i factors, so Y'_j → Y'_i factors through it for large j, and the same argument applied to Y_i → Y_i ×_{Y'_i} Y_i gives injectivity.

Fullness: for f : Y → Y' over X, approximate the quasi-compact open image of its graph by a quasi-compact open immersion V_j ⊂ Y_j ×_{X_j} Y'_j, apply the intermediate step to V_j → Y_j, and compose the inverse with the second projection.

Essential surjectivity: cover a qcqs étale Y → X by quasi-compact opens that descend to a stage — full faithfulness then glues them — and reduce to an f that is a composite of a rational open subset, a finite étale map and a rational open subset, each of which descends by 6.4 (o) and 6.4 (i).

items.name: Tougeron quantitative exact root
items.statement: Let (A,a) be a Noetherian Henselian pair, f₁,…,f_q∈A[X₁,…,X_N], Δ the ideal of q×q Jacobian minors and a₀∈A^N. If f_i(a₀)∈a^n, Δ(a₀)⊃a^h and n>2h, there is b≡a₀ mod a^(n−h) with every f_i(b)=0.
proofSteps: Choose generators t_i of a^h. Adjugates and linear combinations of maximal minors produce matrices N_i with Jac(a₀)N_i=t_i id_q.
Taylor-expand at a₀ with a correction Σ_i t_i u_i. Express f(a₀) using products t_i t_j times coefficients in a^(n−2h). Substitute u_i=Σ_j N_j v_ij.

The resulting auxiliary equations have the form v_ij+Q_ij(v)+c_ij=0 with quadratic Q and c_ij∈a^(n−2h). Their Jacobian is the identity at v=0 modulo that ideal. Localize the determinant, use shared Henselian smooth lifting, and choose v in that ideal. The correction then lies in a^(n−h).

items.name: Elkik conormal stabilization
items.statement: Let A be Noetherian, B=A[X₁,…,X_N]/J with q chosen generators of J, V⊂Spec B smooth over A. Put C=Sym_B(J/J²), with projection π:Spec C→Spec B and zero section. Over π⁻¹V, C is smooth of relative dimension N. Embed Spec C in A_A^(2N+q) by its usual N+q coordinates and N zero coordinates. On every affine open U⊂π⁻¹V, the conormal module of this embedding is free of rank N+q.
proofSteps: Over V the original conormal sequence is split exact, so J/J² is a vector bundle of rank N−d on each relative-dimension-d component. Its symmetric algebra gives a vector bundle of rank N−d over V and hence smooth dimension N.
On an affine U, the differential sequence of the vector bundle splits and Ω_(C/A)|U≃(J/J²)|U⊕Ω_(B/A)|U≃O_U^N. For the N+q-coordinate embedding, its conormal K satisfies K⊕O_U^N≃O_U^(N+q).

Adding N zero coordinates adds O_U^N to K and makes the new conormal free of rank N+q. Finite generation and Nakayama lift a basis to equations on a neighborhood of U. Projection sends an approximating section back to B.

items.name: Elkik approximation over a principal completion
items.statement: Let A be Noetherian and complete for (t), I⊂A an ideal, J⊂A[X₁,…,X_N] finitely generated and H_B⊂H_Jac. Choose k with A[t∞]∩t^kA=0. If H_B(a)⊃(t^h), J(a)⊂t^nI and n>max(2h,h+k), there is b−a∈t^(n−h)I A^N with J(b)=0.
proofSteps: Adjugates for every minor–colon generator give v∈t^nI A^N with Jac(a)v≡t^h f(a) modulo t^(2n)I. Write v=t^hδ with δ∈t^(n−h)I A^N.
The remaining t^h-torsion term lies in t^kA by the exponent inequality, so principal-torsion-separation cancels it at the needed depth. Taylor gives improved error in t^(2n−2h)I.
High congruence preserves the t^h smoothness witness because 1+t z is a unit. Repeat with n↦2n−2h; n>2h makes the exponents diverge. Completeness gives a limit and the original correction bound.

items.name: Elkik approximation over a Noetherian complete pair
items.statement: Let A be Noetherian and a-adically complete, B=A[X₁,…,X_N]/J finite type and H_B⊂H_Jac. For every h there are n₀,r such that n>n₀, H_B(a₀)⊃a^h and J(a₀)⊂a^n imply an exact root b≡a₀ mod a^(n−r).
proofSteps: Induct on the number of generators of an ideal of definition. Choose t₁ and s>max(2h,h+k), where k separates t₁-power torsion. Apply induction modulo t₁^s to produce a′ close to a₀ with J(a′)⊂(t₁^s)∩a^(n−r′).
Use Artin–Rees, or its pinned controlled-preimage theorem for multiplication by t₁^s, to obtain J(a′)⊂t₁^s a^(n−r′−λ). For n large, Nakayama preserves H_B(a′)⊃a^h and hence t₁^h.
Apply the principal complete lemma with I=a^(n−r′−λ); Noetherian a-adic completeness gives the required t₁-adic completeness for t₁∈a. Track the total loss r from r′,λ,s,h.

items.name: Elkik approximation for a principal Henselian pair
items.statement: Let A be Noetherian, (A,(t)) Henselian, B/A finite type and V⊂Spec B smooth over A. Every section over Â whose restriction to D(t) factors through V_Â can, for every n, be approximated modulo t^n by an A-section whose restriction to D(t) lies in V.
proofSteps: Lift the formal section through the zero section of the conormal stabilization; project an eventual solution back. This makes the conormal free on affine smooth opens.

If K cuts out the nonsmooth complement, the formal section pulls K back to an ideal containing t^c. Approximate finitely many coefficients of its witness to choose h∈K with h(σ̂)=t^c(1+t u); thus D(h) contains the formal generic image.
Choose N−d equations f generating J near D(h), replace h by a power so hJ⊂(f), and find a power of t in the evaluated maximal Jacobian minors. Tougeron solves those equations to arbitrary precision.

High congruence preserves the power of t in h at the new point. Its residual J is killed by that power and lies in a sufficiently high t-power ideal. Principal torsion separation makes it zero, and smooth-open-congruence preserves V.
